{"category":"methodology","enforced":false,"name":"Before 1.0, a thing done wrong is CORRECTED, not patched around — compatibility is not a reason to keep a mistake","statement":"WHEN SOMETHING IN REFLOW2 IS WRONG, THE FIX IS THE FULL ONE. A workaround, a compatibility shim, or a repair that leaves the original mistake in place is not the answer while this project is still in development. "It would break consumers" is not, on its own, a reason to keep a defect — it is a reason to do it NOW rather than later.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-17, in his own words: "as we are still in development; I'm more concerned with doing things right. If we did something wrong the first time, it is better to fully correct/fix it now than to do patch or workaround it. I'd rather pay for this change now than when we have hundreds/thousands of users and we can't make big changes out of fear that we may upset something that is working."

⭐ THE COST ARGUMENT RUNS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM THE USUAL INSTINCT, and that is the whole rule. The instinct is that a breaking change is expensive, so defer it. The instinct is right about the price and wrong about the direction of the trend: the price of a break RISES with every consumer, so deferring is buying the same change later at a higher cost, in a currency (user trust, migration effort, fear of touching working code) that is worse than the one it is cheap in now.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not licence to rewrite what merely displeases — the trigger is something WRONG, not something one would style differently. Not licence to widen a task: a correction still gets recorded, tested and reviewed like any change, and `dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key`'s own warning about doing a shape change "under the cover of" finishing something else still stands. The rule changes which OPTION is chosen when a defect is real; it does not change what counts as a defect, and it does not authorise an agent to settle intent (`rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is untouched by it).

WHERE THE HORIZON IS. CHANGELOG.md already says Major/1.0 is "deferred until a stability commitment — the design surface promising compatibility". This rule is the other side of that sentence: until that commitment exists, the surface is explicitly not promising, and behaving as though it were is the mistake. The rule therefore has a natural end — it should be revisited at 1.0 rather than carried into it.

⚠️ WHAT IT ALREADY OVERTURNS, recorded so the reversal is on the record rather than inferred: `dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key` (2026-08-17, hours earlier) declined to rename the `disconnected_community` defect category, on the ground that the key is a consumer contract and renaming it would "break every consumer in order to fix a sentence". Under this rule that ground no longer carries, and the same decision's deferred item — giving unscoped `detect_defects` the same envelope its scoped sibling already returns — moves from deferred to owed.

ENFORCEMENT NOT YET STATED, deliberately. Whether breaking this should stop a build is Anthony's to say, and it is a hard case besides: this rule is about a JUDGEMENT (was the full fix taken?) rather than about graph state, so it may be a genuine instance of a rule no detector can check — the first real customer for `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` alongside `rule:bl-41`."}
